# A Kickstart Guide to Using DataForSEO APIs

![A Kickstart Guide to Using DataForSEO APIs](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/a-kickstart-guide-to-dataforseo-api.jpg)

Table of Contents

While you can’t see them, APIs are everywhere, continuously working in the background to fuel a myriad of digital functionalities that have become essential to our lives.

At DataForSEO, we specialize in APIs that offer a gateway to SEO and marketing data for developers and data enthusiasts alike. We believe that valuable digital insights should be within reach for everyone, so in this article, we provide an accessible starting point for beginners and a comprehensive guide to DataForSEO APIs for experienced users.

This article contains all the necessary information and key resources to consult for streamlined interaction with our APIs. We explain what an API is, give an in-depth overview of how DataForSEO APIs work, and include all the essential steps for making DataForSEO API calls.

### What is an API?

![APIs for SEO software](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/1111api.gif)

An API, short for Application Programming Interface, is a set of rules that facilitates the exchange of information between different software systems, apps, or devices.

#### API examples

Understanding application programming interfaces may be easier with some real-life examples, so let’s consider a few.

- **Stripe API** enables developers to simplify transactions by adding online payment processing services into their apps or software.
- **OpenWeatherMap API** helps to obtain real-time weather data for different locations straight in your app.
- **[DataForSEO’s APIs](https://dataforseo.com/apis)** allow developers and data enthusiasts to access powerful SEO and marketing insights (such as search volume, ranking data, backlink stats, and more) and integrate them into their tools, or platforms.

If you are interested in learning more about APIs for SEO software development, check out [this informative blog post.](https://dataforseo.com/blog/introduction-to-apis-for-seo-software)

#### What are REST APIs

DataForSEO specializes in [REST APIs](https://blog.postman.com/rest-api-examples/). REST, or Representational State Transfer, is the most popular approach to building web APIs based on six principles:

- Uniform interface (UI) – unique resources identifiable through a single URL.
- Client-server model – API clients handle UI and request gathering, while API servers manage data access, workload, and security.
- Stateless operations – each request contains complete client information, while the server doesn’t retain any information about the client state.
- RESTful resource caching – response data is labeled as cacheable or non-cacheable.
- Layered system – hierarchical architecture restricting each component to interact only with its immediate layer.
- Code on demand – the server can return static resources (in XML or JSON) or executable codes as needed.

If some terminology is unclear, don’t worry; we will explain everything step by step in the next parts. The key takeaway is that these principles make a RESTful API service scalable, easily maintainable, flexible, and lightweight.

While other architectural concepts like SOAP and GraphQL exist, this article will focus on REST APIs to provide you with insights into how DataForSEO APIs operate and how to work with them.

### How do APIs work?

At its core, an API acts as an intermediary operating in a request and response cycle between an API client and an API server.

[![dataforseo api client server](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/dataforseo-api-client-server.png)](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/dataforseo-api-client-server.png)

Now that you understand the core principle, let’s delve into the components of REST APIs and learn their roles.

To understand API workflow better, we should first talk about **an API client**. It can be a code or a tool, but either way, an API client is an indispensable component responsible for assembling and sending requests and receiving responses from the API server. It also manages the flow of data (showing it to the user or integrating it into a broader data flow within a software).

**An API request**, also referred to as an API call, is the process during which an API client sends a request to the server and delivers back the server’s response.

**The API server** is one of the indispensable components for API functioning. It is in charge of authentication, validation of input parameters, response data formatting, and the flow of information between the API client and a database.

While the database is not considered an API component, an API cannot operate without it. The API server uses a database to store, manipulate, and extract data that it serves to the API client as a response.

**API response** is the data the API server sends back to the API client following an API request.

If you’re still confused, let’s break it down in simple terms. Imagine you are in a bakery and you (the client) want to get a cake. You don’t need to know the recipe or buy any ingredients, you just approach the shopkeeper (the API) and ask (with an API request) for a chocolate cake. The shopkeeper hands your order to the baker (server or data source). The baker prepares it, and the shopkeeper hands you the ready-made cake. Similarly, accessing valuable data through API ensures a hassle-free experience, much like ordering a cake.

Now, let’s touch on some concepts you should understand when working with DataForSEO APIs.

### Authorization and API key

Commercial APIs commonly require authorization before you can access their functionality, such indicating an API key. To access DataForSEO APIs, you should use your unique **API credentials**, which are a combination of an API login and API password.

 Your **API login** a unique, automatically generated string used to identify your account when making API requests.
 A secure **API password** for API authentication is also automatically generated for you by our system after you create an account.

Note that your API password is intended for authentication when making requests to DataForSEO API and is different from the account password used for dashboard access.

You can always find and request updated DataForSEO API login and password in the [API Access Dashboard section](https://app.dataforseo.com/api-access). Your API login will always remain visible, while your API password and Base64-endcoded credentials **will be hidden 24 hours after registration** for security reasons. If you need them later, you can obtain them via the email address you used for creating an account.

[![new dashboard - api access](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/api-access.png)](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/api-access.png)

### What is an endpoint?

An API endpoint is a specific URL that represents a path for accessing a certain function or resource (e.g. a data set). You may think of an endpoint as a destination explaining to the API server how to proceed with your call.

For example, the following endpoint will tell the API server that you want to do something with the list of locations for Google SERP API:

`https://api.dataforseo.com/v3/serp/google/locations`

However, to tell it exactly what needs to be done, you should also use the appropriate HTTP request method.

### HTTP request methods

HTTP request methods indicate what operations should be performed by following the path you indicate as an endpoint. When working with DataForSEO APIs, you will be using only POST and GET methods.

The GET method allows you to retrieve data from the specified endpoint. Additionally, in some cases, the POST method ensures an enhanced user experience by allowing you to pass your data extraction parameters to our system and facilitating the retrieval of [Live](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/live-vs-standard-method) task results.

Whenever you make an API request, always check and use the appropriate HTTP method for each endpoint. This information is set by default in our [Postman collection and examples for PHP, Python, and C#.](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/?bash) You can also find the appropriate HTTP method indicated before the endpoint’s URL in our documentation.

[![kickstart dataforseo api guide](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/kickstart-dataforseo-api-guide-1.png)](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/kickstart-dataforseo-api-guide-1.png)

For instance, to retrieve the list of locations available for Google SERP API, you should use the GET method. At the same time, to extract top 100 Google SERP results with either [Live or Standard data delivery](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/live-vs-standard-method), you should use a POST call and include endpoint-specific data extraction parameters in the request body.

### Request body and JSON parameters

The request body (also called task body or payload) is a section of an HTTP request containing data (parameters). Parameters are the variables or fields intended for specifying your data processing instructions.

When making calls to DataForSEO API, all data in your request body should be sent in JSON format. [JSON](https://www.json.org/json-en.html) keeps its data in name-value pairs. We’ll provide an example further.

First, let’s consider the parameters more closely. In our documentation, you will see that some parameters are **required** while others are *optional*.

Required fields mean that your API request cannot be processed if your request body does not contain them. For example, you want to make a POST request for processing some Google Search results using this endpoint: `https://api.dataforseo.com/v3/serp/google/organic/task_post`

Your API call instructions will only be understood by the API server if they include three **required** parameters specifying the keyword, location, and language you are interested in. Here’s an example of a POST request body containing these parameters.

```
[
    {
        "language_name": "English",
        "location_name": "United States",
        "keyword": "albert einstein"
    }
]
```

You can easily understand the name-value relationship in JSON here. The name `"language_name"` has a value of `"English"`.

You can always find all available POST parameters and instructions for specifying them on the endpoint’s documentation page. For instance, here’s a page describing parameters for [Setting Google Organic SERP Tasks.](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/serp/google/organic/task_post/?bash)

As for optional fields, you can simply omit them in the body of your API requests. However, **note that some optional parameters will be set to default values if you do not specify otherwise**. For example, if you do not indicate a device type (desktop or mobile) for which you want to check the search results, the API will return data for the desktop by default.

You will find default values for every optional request parameter in their description on the documentation page of the related endpoint.

There are also optional fields that do not have any default values and do not impact the data you receive in the results. For instance, if you do not use a `tag` parameter (which can indicate a custom task identifier in your system), the data you retrieve simply will not contain it.

### Non-technical guidelines for making DataForSEO API calls using Postman

1 Download and install the [Postman](https://www.postman.com/) tool. [Download POSTMAN Examples](https://cdn.dataforseo.com/v3/examples/dataforseo_xmpl_v3_postman.zip?2024123) and import the unarchived JSON file into the tool.

[![kickstart dataforseo api guide 2.1](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/kickstart-dataforseo-api-guide-2.1.png)](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/kickstart-dataforseo-api-guide-2.1.png)

2 Open the DataForSEO collection, and select the API endpoint from it. For example, you can go to the *Keyword Data API* folder, select *Google Ads*, and head to the *keywords_for_site* folder. Launch the *task_post* or *live* endpoint.

[![kickstart dataforseo api guide 3](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/kickstart-dataforseo-api-guide-3.png)](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/kickstart-dataforseo-api-guide-3.png)

3 Specify your API login and password in the *Auth* tab.

[![kickstart dataforseo api guide 4](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/kickstart-dataforseo-api-guide-4.png)](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/kickstart-dataforseo-api-guide-4.png)

4 If you are making a POST request, add POST parameters to the *Body* of your request. Make sure to include all parameters marked as required on the selected endpoint’s page [in our docs.](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/?bash) You can also make a request with the parameters already included in the example.

[![kickstart dataforseo api guide 5](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/kickstart-dataforseo-api-guide-5.png)](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/kickstart-dataforseo-api-guide-5.png)

5 Hit *Send* to submit your API request.

6 Wait for the response from our API. If you are using the Live method, you will obtain the data you requested in the API response.

If you are using the Standard method, the API response will provide you with the ID of the task you set. You should then copy the ID and proceed to the next step.

[![kickstart dataforseo api guide 6](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/kickstart-dataforseo-api-guide-6.png)](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/kickstart-dataforseo-api-guide-6.png)

[➤ Learn more about task ID.](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/whats-task-id)
[➤ Learn more about the difference between Live and Standard methods.](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/live-vs-standard-method)

7 Select the appropriate GET endpoint for collecting the task results, e.g. launch the *task_get* from the *keywords_for_site* folder. Replace the example ID at the end of the request URL after `task_get/` with the ID of your task.

[![kickstart dataforseo api guide 7](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/kickstart-dataforseo-api-guide-7.png)](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/kickstart-dataforseo-api-guide-7.png)

8 Once again, specify your API login and password in the Auth tab.

9 Submit your API request by hitting *Send*, and wait for the response from our API.

[![kickstart dataforseo api guide 8](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/kickstart-dataforseo-api-guide-8.jpg)](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/kickstart-dataforseo-api-guide-8.jpg)

The structure of the response body varies depending on the specific DataForSEO API endpoint and the type of data you are requesting.

You can always refer to the [DataForSEO documentation](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/?bash) to find the necessary endpoint and review an example of its response body structure (lower right section with JSON code) along with a detailed description of the fields the response can contain organized into a handy table.

In case your request returns an error in the `status_code` and `status_message` fields, refer to the [Errors endpoint](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/appendix/errors/?bash) of our documentation for instructions, or contact our support team.

**Tip**: After you hit Send, and receive a response, use the built-in **Visualize** button. This option allows you to create tables, charts, and graphs based on the API response data, making it easy to spot trends and gain insights at a glance.

[![postman - visualize api response](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/postman-visualize-api-response.png)](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/postman-visualize-api-response.png)

**See also: the list of useful resources.**

### Developer guidelines for making requests to DataForSEO API

1 Get an API client. You can create your REST client or use one of the ready-made, officially supported clients for PHP, Python, C#, Java, and TypeScript – listed [here in our documentation.](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/?bash)

2 Regardless of the programming language, your unique API credentials should be passed in the ‘Authorization’ header within the request in the following format:

`Authorization: Basic login:password`

Instead of “login” and “password”, use your API login and password encoded in Base64. You can find your DataForSEO API login and password, as well the Base64-encoded string in the [API Access section of the Dashboard.](https://app.dataforseo.com/api-access)

For more information about Authentication for making DataForSEO API calls, refer to [our documentation.](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/auth/?bash)

3 Indicate the URL of the API endpoint of your choice. You can copy it from [our documentation](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/?bash), e.g. `https://api.dataforseo.com/v3/serp/google/organic/task_post`

4 Set the appropriate HTTP method (POST/GET). It’s indicated before the URL of the endpoint in [our docs.](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/?bash)

5 If you are making a POST request, add POST parameters to the body of your request. All data in your request body should be sent in the JSON format (UTF-8 encoding). Include all parameters marked as required in our documentation. Make sure the request body is valid. You can find an example body in the upper right section of the selected endpoint’s page in our docs.

**See also: the list of useful resources with guides for results polling, using pingbacks & postbacks.**

6 If you are making a GET request to obtain the results of a set task, replace $id at the end of the request URL with the ID of your task.

7 Submit your API request.

8 Wait for the response from our API.

If you are setting a task using a Task POST endpoint, save the ID of the task provided in the response. You can use it repeatedly within 30 days to retrieve the results of the task.

If you collect the results of a set task, you can always refer to the [DataForSEO documentation](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/?bash) to find the necessary endpoint and review an example of its response body structure (lower right section with JSON code) along with a detailed description of the fields the response can contain.

Here are some important components of an API response you should know about when working with DataForSEO API.

#### DataForSEO status codes and messages

Alongside general HTTP status codes, our system also generates internal API response status codes and messages. They are provided in the response body, e.g.:

```
"status_code": 20100,
"status_message": "Task Created.",
```

The `status_code` and `status_message` parameters indicated after the `version` in the response describe the status of your API call, while the `status_code` and `status_message` provided in the array of `tasks` describe the status of a particular task.

The `status_code` fields of a successful request and a successfully set task indicated in the response body will meet the following condition: 20000 <= `status_code` <= 29999. Refer to the [Errors endpoint](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/appendix/errors/?bash) of our documentation to get the full list of DataForSEO’s internal status codes and messages.

#### HTTP response headers

The following response headers are essential for understanding and managing your DataForSEO API requests:

**X-RateLimit-Limit** indicates the rate limit ceiling per minute for the given API endpoint. Each DataForSEO API has a certain rate limit. If your system requires increased limits, please contact our support team via chat.

**X-RateLimit-Remaining** states the number of requests remaining in the current rate limit window.

**Content-Encoding** provides the encoding format of the response data. By default, DataForSEO API responses are compressed with gzip if you use one of the API clients listed [here in our docs.](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/?bash)

**Content-Type** indicates the data format in the response body. All DataForSEO API responses are returned in JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) format by default.

We also support responses in the XML (Extensible Markup Language) format – just append `.xml` to the end of your request URL. In addition to that, you can request HTML (Hypertext Markup Language) data from endpoints that return HTML-encoded results by appending `.html` to the end of the request URL.

For example, the following requests will return a response encoded in XML or HTML respectively:

`https://api.dataforseo.com/v3/appendix/user_data.xml`
`https://api.dataforseo.com/v3/serp/google/organic/task_get/html/09061543-1535-0066-0000-6240830f56ba.html`

#### Note on request limits

In general, you can send up to 10,000 API calls per minute. If your project requires increased limits, please contact our support team.

Note that rate limits may vary per API. We recommend checking our documentation for a specific API and endpoint to learn all the details beforehand.

### Integration with no-code platforms

At DataForSEO, we aim to offer our API users the maximum flexibility and accessibility. That’s why we created numerous options to leverage the power of our APIs with [no-code platforms and AI tools.](https://dataforseo.com/integrations) By integrating DataForSEO APIs in no-code applications, you can turn complex marketing processes into seamless, automated workflows. From data-driven keyword research to comprehensive domain analysis, you can automate a lot without deep technical knowledge.

*Want to see that in action? Our free **SEO API Basics** course walks you through all you need to know to confidently use APIs and connect them to n8n, Make, and AI agents: 9 lessons, ~35 minutes. **[Start the free course →](https://academy.dataforseo.com/api-basics?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=ac_basics&utm_id=academy)***

#### What are no-code platforms?

No-code platforms are special applications designed to create simple digital workflows, automate processes, and store data by integrating and connecting multiple third-party solutions. Such platforms are flexible and easy to use, requiring little to no coding experience.

DataForSEO APIs can seamlessly integrate into no-code platforms like Make and Airtable and serve as data sources or analysis tools for workflows. Such integrations allow everyone to create comprehensive marketing automations powered by quality data – in one go.

#### Which no-code solutions can you integrate DataForSEO APIs with?

1 **[DataForSEO Google Sheets Connector](https://dataforseo.com/google-sheets-connector)**. This is [our proprietary Google Chrome extension](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/dataforseo_api_connector/630215580340) that connects DataForSEO APIs to Google Sheets, creating an extensive SEO toolkit that you can leverage without a single line of code.

[![DFS-Connector-Integration-Guide](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/DFS-Connector-Integration-Guide.webp)](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/DFS-Connector-Integration-Guide.webp)

The SEO tools featured in the Google Sheets Connector are based on DataForSEO APIs, such as [SERP API](https://dataforseo.com/apis/serp-api), [DataForSEO Labs API](https://dataforseo.com/apis/dataforseo-labs-api), [Keywords Data API](https://dataforseo.com/apis/keyword-data-api), [Backlinks API](https://dataforseo.com/apis/backlinks-api), [OnPage API](https://dataforseo.com/apis/on-page-api), and more. Using the Google Sheets interface, the Connector significantly simplifies the work with such APIs. Moreover, all data is pulled directly into the datasheets, meaning that you don’t need to scrape it from JSON responses manually – you can instantly access it for analysis.

To access Google Sheets Connector, [register at DataForSEO](https://app.dataforseo.com/register), install [the extension](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/dataforseo_api_connector/630215580340), and follow [our comprehensive guide](https://dataforseo.com/blog/google-sheets-connector-v3) to complete integration.

2 **[Make](https://dataforseo.com/make-integration)**. This revolutionary visual automation platform integrates multiple popular apps to create seamless workflows and custom solutions. The main advantage of the Make platform is its functionality and user-friendly interface. You can create automation scenarios using drag-and-drop modules, connecting numerous tools simultaneously.

![Make-Integration-Guide](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Make-Integration-Guide.webp)

DataForSEO APIs can be easily integrated into Make as customizable modules for creating data-driven SEO and marketing workflows. The number of tools and automation you can create using DataForSEO modules is up to your imagination. For example, you can assemble [a fully automated domain analysis app](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/simple-domain-analysis-app-with-dataforseo-api-make) or [brand mention monitoring tool](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/automated-mention-tracking-with-api-in-make) that sends mention updates directly to your email. To create scenarios, you can use pre-built DataForSEO modules based on our APIs or make custom API calls with the “Make an API Call” module.

Integrating DataForSEO APIs with Make is simple. First, [sign up for a DataForSEO account](https://app.dataforseo.com/register) to obtain your API credentials, then [create a Make account](https://www.make.com/en/register). Next, select a DataForSEO module in the scenario dashboard, connect it to Make, and start building your workflows!

3 **[Airtable](https://dataforseo.com/airtable-integration)**. This cloud collaboration service combines the functionality of datasheets and advanced databases to automate complex data collection and analysis processes. It offers a user-friendly interface where information is stored in tables, similar to spreadsheets, but with the added functionality of a relational database. This concept allows for assembling unique automation and data processing scenarios, perfect for creating tailored SEO and marketing tools with APIs.

![Airtable-Integration-Guide](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Airtable-Integration-Guide.webp)

Inside Airtable, you can create a custom table with specific columns, update triggers, and automation setups as a base for your tailored SEO tool. Then, by installing and configuring the DataForSEO Airtable extension, you can easily fetch DataForSEO API data into your datasheet. The data can be stored conveniently, regularly updated, and analyzed. You can also copy our [pre-configured Airtable database](https://airtable.com/appcWDTFqRDUyzfhF/shrxi0CbcDIuaE3i2) to facilitate the integration of DataForSEO APIs.

To get started with Airtable, first [obtain your API credentials](https://app.dataforseo.com/register) and log into your [Airtable account](https://airtable.com/login). Then, customize your table or download [a pre-configured one](https://airtable.com/appcWDTFqRDUyzfhF/shrxi0CbcDIuaE3i2), install the DataForSEO extension, and start using your tool.

**See also:** [Integrating Search Volume Data into Airtable with Keyword Data API](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/search-volume-in-airtable-with-keyword-data-api)

4 **[Zapier](https://dataforseo.com/zapier-integration)**. This cloud-based automation platform enables users to connect and automate tasks between over 7,000 web applications without requiring coding skills. By creating so-called “Zaps,” you can set up workflows where an event in one app triggers an action in another, streamlining processes and reducing manual work. Zapier is perfect for creating low-level automated workflows involving multiple actions across various services, including DataForSEO.

![Zapier-Integration](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Zapier-Integration-1500x810.webp)

In Zapier, you can integrate DataForSEO APIs into your workflows as custom actions that are triggered by specific events. For example, you can set up an automated workflow to retrieve search volume for specified keywords from the [Keywords Data API](https://dataforseo.com/apis/keyword-data-api) and add the data directly to your Google Sheet. Additionally, you can simplify workflow creation by using ready-to-use Zapier templates, such as “[Update new Airtable records with Google SERP positions](https://zapier.com/apps/airtable/integrations/airtable/1818703/update-new-airtable-records-with-google-serp-positions-from-dataforseo)”.

Similar to previous integrations, you can easily start using DataForSEO APIs directly in Zapier. Simply obtain your API credentials [from your DataForSEO account](https://app.dataforseo.com/register), [register on Zapier](https://zapier.com/sign-up), and begin building your automation with custom actions or pre-made workflows.

5 **[Official node in n8n.](https://dataforseo.com/n8n-integration)** **n8n** is a powerful, open-source workflow automation tool that allows connecting various apps, APIs, and databases with minimal coding. It’s the perfect option for developers and businesses who need full control over their data and automation logic. The DataForSEO n8n node includes a wide set of actions, based on our most popular APIs, giving you the flexibility to automate virtually any SEO and marketing workflow in n8n in just a few minutes.

[![use node n8n dataforseo](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/use-node-n8n-dataforseo-e1771001369870.png)](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/use-node-n8n-dataforseo-e1771001369870.png)

6 **[DataForSEO MCP Server](https://dataforseo.com/model-context-protocol)**. It’s the DataForSEO implementation of the Model Context Protocol. Basically, it’s a bridge between AI models and DataForSEO APIs, helping you to easily extract data and turn it into insights without writing a single line of code.

[![MCP Request 1](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/MCP-Request-1.gif)](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/MCP-Request-1.gif)

To connect the MCP Server to Claude, for instance, follow **[this simple guide on our Help Center](https://dataforseo.com/help-center/connect-claude-to-dataforseo-mcp-very-simple-guide)** or **[this video tutorial.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4C6dgxiQIpY)**

We continuously expand our API integration solutions with new options and no-code platforms. Check out [our dedicated blog post](https://dataforseo.com/blog/create-custom-low-level-marketing-automation-solutions-with-dataforseo-apis) for more information on no-code API solutions.

### Summary

In summary, APIs enable seamless interaction between software systems. The main API components include the API client, API call, API server, and API response. DataForSEO’s REST APIs provide a streamlined way to access SEO and marketing data.

To make a successful DataForSEO API call, use the correct API credentials for authorization, and include all required request body parameters in POST calls.

For the Live method of data delivery, the data you request is provided in the API response to a single POST call. The more affordable Standard data delivery method requires setting a task with a POST call and making a separate GET request to obtain the results. It has two priorities, Normal and High, determining the speed of data collection. To retrieve results through a GET request, you should append a task ID at the end of the request URL.

To understand and properly process the API response, you should check the response body containing task results (requested data), task ID(s), or an error message.

Whenever necessary, you can consult our [documentation](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/?bash) for details on JSON parameters available for sending requests and API response fields of the endpoint you are using.

For handling related exceptional or error conditions, refer to the [Errors endpoint](https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/appendix/errors/?bash) of our documentation, or contact our support team for assistance.
